text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince Hassan calls on Arab political parties meeting in Amman to overcome their past complexes. Calls for establishment of a centre qualified to resolve conflicts.
- Head of Jordanian committee for Gulf War compensation says the United Nations approved 2,389 of the 2,400 Jordanian claims in the under-$100,000 category.
- King Hussein and Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak discuss the situation in the Middle East on the phone.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti says the consequences of Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Israeli closure of Palestinian territories is catastrophic.
- Consumer association will next week offer Ramadan (Moslem fasting month) supplies at cost price.
- Kabariti meets Tunisian Prime Minister Hamed Karoui. Joint news conference reveals complementary views towards a number of issues.
- Deputy Prime Minister Ensour denies in parliament that Islamists are barred from Foreign Ministry.
- Returnees from Kuwait to get compensation in February.
- Jordan's security is the first to be affected by Israel's "explosive" policies of intensifying settlements in the West Bank.
- A move to cancel customs on mobile telephones to encouarge investments.
- Stocks decline in the Amman Financial Market and bloc sales at the value of 1.6 million dinars ($2.3 million) prop up turnover.
